A commercial customer organization that holds one or more licenses to our products and is entitled to receive support. The Account is the unit that entitlement, licensing, regional assignment and commercial ownership all hang off. An Account is an organization, never an individual person - the people at an account are modelled as `sup:Contact`.
column7: Ontology class sup:Account (Customer). Identity: The CRM account ID is authoritative. Where an organization exists as multiple account records across brand-specific CRM orgs, they are the same `sup:Account` only if they share a resolved parent organization ID. See `OQ-03` - account de-duplication across brand orgs is unresolved. Known aliases: Account, Customer, Organization, Org.

column4: An individual person at a customer account who is authorised to raise support tickets and use self-service tools. A Contact is a person in their capacity as a customer representative. Internal staff are modelled as `sup:SupportAgent`, `sup:SalesRepresentative` or `sup:CustomerSuccessManager`.
column7: Ontology class sup:Contact (Customer). Identity: CRM contact ID is authoritative. Known aliases: Contact, Requester, Reporter, Submitter.

column4: A customer relationship management system that records tickets. Each distinct CRM instance is a distinct instance of this class, because each carries its own ticket numbering, its own user records, and - critically - its own vocabulary.
column7: Ontology class sup:CRM (Support). Identity: Natural key: the system code (e.g. `SF_EMEA`, `SF_AMER`). Each org is a separate instance even when several orgs run on the same platform, because the ID spaces and the vocabulary do not carry across. Known aliases: Org, Instance, Tenant, Source, System of record, Upstream, Salesforce, "the system".

column4: An internal individual assigned to accounts considered valuable, with responsibility for adoption, retention and relationship health. Unlike the sales representative, CSM assignment is conditional - most accounts do not have one.
column7: Ontology class sup:CustomerSuccessManager (Customer). Identity: The CRM user ID is authoritative. Known aliases: CSM, Customer Success Manager, Success owner, TAM, Technical account manager (may be a distinct role - OQ-36).

column4: Published product documentation and knowledge base content that support agents consult to resolve tickets. One instance is one published unit - an article or page - identified by its URL.
column7: Ontology class sup:Documentation (Knowledge). Identity: The published URL is authoritative. Where content exists at several URLs (localised or mirrored), the canonical URL is the identity and the others are recorded as aliases. Known aliases: Article, KB article, Doc, Page, The docs, the wiki, Content, Topic.

column4: The act of a support agent referring a ticket to development because it has been identified as a defect or as a request for new functionality. The Escalation produces a Jira issue and is the only legitimate way a Jira ID becomes associated with a ticket.
column7: Ontology class sup:Escalation (Support). Identity: Surrogate: generated UUID. There is no natural key - the same ticket can be escalated more than once, and the same Jira issue can receive escalations from many tickets. Known aliases: Bug report, Dev handoff, "raising a Jira", Escalation flag, Escalated case.

column4: A unit of engineering work tracked in Jira, created as the result of a support escalation, representing either a defect to fix or a capability to build. Its key is the identifier that gets associated back to the originating ticket.
column7: Ontology class sup:JiraIssue (Engineering). Identity: The Jira issue key (e.g. `PROJ-1234`) is authoritative and globally unique. Known aliases: Jira, Jira ID, ticket (dangerous - see below), Issue, Story, Bug, Defect, Jira reference, Dev ID.

column4: A grant of the right to use a specific product, held by a specific account, for a defined period and quantity. The license is what makes a support request legitimate: an account may only raise tickets about products it is licensed for.
column7: Ontology class sup:License (Customer). Identity: Composite: `accountId` + `productId` + `startDate`. A renewal produces a new License instance rather than mutating the existing one, so that historical coverage questions stay answerable. Known aliases: Asset, Entitlement key, Serial, Subscription.

column4: An Independent Software Vendor (ISV) or partner organization that represents one or more accounts. Partners can submit and manage support tickets on behalf of the customers they represent.
column7: Ontology class sup:Partner (Customer). Identity: The CRM partner ID is authoritative. Known aliases: Partner / ISV.

column4: A software product that customers license and raise support tickets about. The Product is what a license grants access to, what a ticket concerns, and what documentation describes. It is the join point between the commercial, support and knowledge parts of the model.
column7: Ontology class sup:Product (Product). Identity: The licensing system product ID is authoritative. Version is not part of identity - a product and its versions are the same product. Version-specific facts would need `sup:ProductVersion`, which is not modelled (`OQ-15`). Known aliases: SKU, Part number, Product2, Asset product, Product, Component, Product folder, Product line, Product family.

column4: A geographic territory used to distribute accounts and assign commercial and support coverage. Regions determine which sales representative owns an account and which support team's working hours apply to its tickets.
column7: Ontology class sup:Region (Customer). Identity: Natural key: the region code (`EMEA`, `NA`, `APAC`, `LATAM`). Codes are stable and never reused. Known aliases: Territory, Geo, Coverage zone.

column4: An internal individual who commercially owns a set of accounts. Assignment is driven by region: an account's sales representative is drawn from the representatives covering that account's region.
column7: Ontology class sup:SalesRepresentative (Customer). Identity: The CRM user ID is authoritative. Known aliases: Account owner, Owner, AE, Account executive, Rep, Renewal owner (may be a different person - see OQ-34).

column4: The graded measure of a ticket's business impact and urgency, used to set response expectations and routing. Every ticket has exactly one.
column7: Ontology class sup:SeverityLevel (Support). Identity: Natural key: the canonical level code `S1`-`S4`. All product-specific labels (`P1`, `Critical`, `High`, `1 - Urgent`) resolve to one of these four. Known aliases: Severity, Sev, Priority, Pri, Impact, Urgency (informal, not a field).

column4: The Service Level Agreement that governs a ticket, dictating the target times for response and resolution. An SLA is determined by the severity of the ticket and the entitlement of the customer account. Support agents are measured against their ability to meet these SLA targets.
column7: Ontology class sup:SLA (Support). Identity: A composite of `severityLevel` + `entitlementTier`. Known aliases: Service Level Agreement, SLA.

column4: An internal member of the support organization who is assigned tickets, resolves them using documentation, and escalates to development when a ticket is caused by a defect or requires new functionality.
column7: Ontology class sup:SupportAgent (Support). Identity: The CRM user ID is authoritative. Agents appearing in more than one CRM are matched on corporate email. Known aliases: Case owner, Assigned to, Owner, Support engineer, Technical support, Analyst, T1, T2, T3 agent.

column4: The tier of support service an account is entitled to receive. The tier governs response time targets, escalation rights and channel access. Entitlement is a property of the account, not of an individual ticket or license.
column7: Ontology class sup:SupportEntitlement (Customer). Identity: Natural key: the canonical tier code (`STANDARD`, `PREMIUM`). Entitlement is a controlled vocabulary, not a per-account record - the per-account fact is the `hasEntitlement` link, and its effective dates live on the link. Known aliases: Support Level, Support Plan, Entitlement, Premium Support, Platinum Support, Standard Support, Basic (unverified).

column4: A single recorded request for support from a customer account, tracked from submission to resolution. One ticket represents one customer problem. It is owned by exactly one account, assigned to at most one agent at a time, carries exactly one severity, is governed by exactly one SLA, and may be escalated to development. It may be submitted by a Contact at the account or, where the customer buys through one, by a Partner acting on the account's behalf.
column7: Ontology class sup:Ticket (Support). Identity: The CRM ticket/case number is authoritative. Ticket numbers are unique within a CRM but not across CRMs - a fully qualified ticket identity is `systemCode` + `ticketNumber`. This is a real collision risk in reporting. Known aliases: Case, Incident, SR, Service Request.
